about.title: Maywood Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Maywood is a small city, but its density of warehouses, trucking operations, and small manufacturing sites along corridors like Atlantic Boulevard and Pine Avenue means workers face real risks every shift. Most job injuries here go through California's workers' compensation system, which pays medical care and partial wage replacement without needing to prove fault. But comp isn't always the whole story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate claim outside the comp system. This matters in Maywood especially for delivery drivers and warehouse staff who work around vehicles and machinery owned by companies other than their employer. Our team handles both workers' comp cases and third-party injury claims. We review your paperwork, explain your options, and tell you honestly whether a third-party claim is worth pursuing alongside your comp benefits. There is no fee unless you recover.

items.title: Understanding the 30-Day Report Window
items.desc: California requires injured employees to notify their employer within 30 days of a workplace injury to preserve workers' comp eligibility. We can help you confirm this was done correctly or address it if it wasn't.

items.title: Spotting Third-Party Claims Beyond Comp
items.desc: Because workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, it's easy to miss that a negligent third party, like a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker, may owe you a separate claim. We can evaluate whether your Maywood workplace injury involves other liable parties.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report injuries or file comp claims. If you're worried about your job status after getting hurt, we can help you understand your protections.

items.question: I was hurt driving a delivery route near Atlantic Boulevard for my employer. Is that covered by workers' comp?
items.answer: Generally yes, injuries during work-related driving are typically covered by workers' comp regardless of fault. However, if another driver caused the crash, you may also have a separate third-party injury claim against that driver. We can look at the specifics of your route and the crash to sort out which claims apply.

items.question: Can I sue my employer directly for my workplace injury in Maywood?
items.answer: In most cases, no, workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault. The exception is when a third party, not your employer, contributed to your injury, such as a subcontractor or equipment manufacturer. We can review your situation to see if a third-party claim is available.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim if a third party caused my workplace injury?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of injury. This is separate from the workers' comp reporting timeline, so it's worth getting an evaluation sooner rather than later. Waiting too long can limit your options.
